transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah… um, I guess what brings me in is that I’ve been having these nights where I kind of don’t feel in control around food. It’s usually after work, or sometimes after dinner if it’s been tense or stressful, and I’ll start eating something, and then it’s like… I don’t know how to explain it exactly, but the part of me that makes decisions just sort of shuts off.

I can see myself doing it, like I’m watching myself reach for more, and I know I should stop or at least pause, but I can’t seem to make myself stop in the moment. It feels strange saying it out loud because it sounds simple, like “just stop eating,” but when it’s happening, it doesn’t feel simple at all. It feels like I’m already in motion and I can’t interrupt it.
Can you describe how long these episodes of feeling out of control around food typically last when they happen?

Usually it’s not the whole night, exactly. It feels like forever when I’m in it, but if I’m being honest it’s probably more like an hour, maybe two hours on a really bad night.

Like, I’ll have a normal dinner or there’ll be leftovers, and I’ll tell myself I’m just going to heat up a plate. But then I can eat the full plate, and instead of being done I’ll keep standing in the kitchen, going back and forth. Bread, random snacks, ice cream if it’s there… just one thing after another. And it’s way more than I’d ever eat if someone were sitting there with me. If my wife or a friend were in the room, I’d be embarrassed and I don’t think I’d do it that way.

So, yeah… typically it’s contained to maybe an hour or two, but during that time it feels really out of control.
After these episodes, do you find yourself feeling guilty, ashamed, or upset about what happened?

I mean… I’m not totally sure how to answer that in a clean way. I don’t think I’ve really sat down and named it as guilt or shame exactly, if that makes sense.

Afterward I usually just feel… off. Like I sort of want to avoid thinking about it, and I’ll tell myself it wasn’t that big of a deal or that I was just hungry or tired. Sometimes I’m upset with myself, but I also try not to linger on it because then it turns into this whole mental spiral. So I don’t know if I’d say it’s always guilt or shame, but it definitely doesn’t feel good afterward.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever try to compensate for what you've eaten, like making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Yeah… um. I guess this is the part I don’t really like saying.

There have been times, not every time, but enough that I can’t honestly say no, where afterward I’ll wait until everyone’s gone to bed and then I’ll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up. I’ll tell myself in the moment that I’m just… undoing it, I guess. Like if I can get rid of some of it then maybe the whole thing didn’t really happen, or I didn’t do as much damage as it feels like I did.

And sometimes it’s not throwing up, it’s laxatives. I don’t even feel good about saying that because it sounds so deliberate, and it is, but in my head at the time I make it sound practical or necessary. Like, “Okay, I just need to fix this.” But afterward I usually feel embarrassed, and kind of shaky, and then I’m standing there thinking, “What am I doing?” So… yeah, that has happened.
How often do these episodes of feeling out of control around food happen? Like, how many times a week or month would you say this occurs?

It’s been… most weeks, I’d say. I wish I could say it was more occasional than that, but over the last few months there’s usually at least one night in a week where it happens — where I get into that out-of-control eating thing and then afterwards I’m trying to make up for it somehow.

Sometimes that means I make myself throw up, sometimes it’s laxatives, and other times I’ll tell myself I’m going to “balance it out” by not eating the next meal or by forcing myself to take a really long walk even if I’m tired and don’t actually want to. It’s not like every single day, and it’s not always the exact same pattern, but if you asked me honestly, most weeks there’s been one of those nights. Maybe some weeks it doesn’t happen, but lately it’s been regular enough that I’ve started sort of anticipating it, which feels awful to admit.
